bibl.title: Reporting guidelines for clinical trial reports for interventions involving artificial intelligence: the CONSORT-AI extension

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: A CONTROLLED VOCABULARY BUILT BY VOTE - 14 required disclosures for a trial of an AI intervention, chosen from 41 candidates by a two-round Delphi of 103 stakeholders and a 31-person consensus meeting with a pre-specified 80% inclusion threshold
span.quote: The CONSORT-AI extension recommends that 14 new checklists items be added to the existing CONSORT 2010 statement (11 extensions and 3 elaborations). These items were considered sufficiently important for clinical-trial reports for AI interventions that they should be routinely reported in addition to the core CONSORT 2010 checklist items.

span.label: which AI-specific facts must appear in a clinical trial report before that report can be critically appraised, and which of them command consensus
span.quote: It has been recognized that most recent AI studies are inadequately reported and existing reporting guidelines do not fully cover potential sources of bias specific to AI systems

span.label: the CONSORT-AI checklist: 11 extension and 3 elaboration items added to CONSORT 2010, with a glossary defining the terms they use
span.quote: The CONSORT-AI extension recommends that 14 new checklists items be added to the existing CONSORT 2010 statement (11 extensions and 3 elaborations). These items were considered sufficiently important for clinical-trial reports for AI interventions that they should be routinely reported in addition to the core CONSORT 2010 checklist items.

span.label: method
span.quote: The CONSORT-AI extension recommends that 14 new checklists items be added to the existing CONSORT 2010 statement (11 extensions and 3 elaborations). These items were considered sufficiently important for clinical-trial reports for AI interventions that they should be routinely reported in addition to the core CONSORT 2010 checklist items.

span.label: reporting completeness as something that must be defined term by term, voted on, and published as a list
span.quote: It is important to note that these are minimum requirements and there may be value in including additional items not included in the checklists in the report or in supplementary materials

span.label: staged consensus: literature review and expert consultation to generate 29 candidate items, a two-stage Delphi survey (103 then 91 respondents), a two-day consensus meeting with anonymous electronic voting, and a 34-participant checklist pilot
span.term: staged consensus: literature review and expert consultation to generate 29 candidate items, a two-stage Delphi survey (103 then 91 respondents), a two-day consensus meeting with anonymous electronic voting, and a 34-participant checklist pilot
span.quote: 103 responses were received for the first Delphi round, and 91 responses (88% of participants from round one) were received for the second round. The results of the Delphi survey informed the subsequent international consensus meeting. 12 new items were proposed by the Delphi study participants and were added for discussion at the consensus meeting.

span.label: THE GLOSSARY DEFINES TWO TERMS IDENTICALLY. `Health outcome: MEASURED VARIABLES IN THE TRIAL **THAT** ARE USED TO ASSESS THE EFFECTS OF AN INTERVENTION.` `Clinical outcome: MEASURED VARIABLES IN THE TRIAL **WHICH** ARE USED TO ASSESS THE EFFECTS OF AN INTERVENTION.` Word-diffed rather than eyeballed: the only difference is `that` vs `which`. Two entries, one definition, in a vocabulary whose purpose is precision
span.quote: Health outcome Measured variables in the trial that are used to assess the effects of an intervention. Human–AI interaction The process of how users (humans) interact with the AI intervention, for the AI intervention to function as intended. Clinical outcome Measured variables in the trial which are used to assess the effects of an intervention.

span.label: AND ONE TERM'S DEFINITION HANDS THE DEFINING BACK TO THE READER: `Performance error: Instances in which the AI intervention fails to perform as expected. This term can describe different types of failures, and IT IS UP TO THE INVESTIGATOR TO SPECIFY WHAT SHOULD BE CONSIDERED A PERFORMANCE ERROR, preferably based on prior evidence.` A deliberately open slot in a controlled vocabulary - the opposite move to a threshold, and made on purpose
span.quote: Performance error Instances in which the AI intervention fails to perform as expected. This term can describe different types of failures, and it is up to the investigator to specify what should be considered a performance error, preferably based on prior evidence.

span.label: AND THE `SPIRIT-AI` ENTRY CARRIES A DIFFERENT TERM'S DEFINITION: it reads `An additional checklist item to address AI-specific content that is not adequately covered by SPIRIT 2013` - which is the `CONSORT-AI EXTENSION ITEM` definition with SPIRIT and 2013 substituted, word for word by difflib. `SPIRIT-AI EXTENSION ITEM` does not appear anywhere in the paper, while `SPIRIT-AI elaboration item` sits in the next entry. THE INITIATIVE'S NAME HAS BEEN GIVEN ITS OWN CHECKLIST ITEM'S DEFINITION
span.quote: SPIRIT Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials. SPIRIT-AI An additional checklist item to address AI-specific content that is not adequately covered by SPIRIT 2013. SPIRIT-AI elaboration item Additional considerations to an existing SPIRIT 2013 item when applied to AI interventions.

span.label: AND A THRESHOLD HELD WHILE THE ITEM MOVED UNTIL IT PASSED: `An 80% THRESHOLD FOR INCLUSION WAS PRE-SPECIFIED`, and `CONSORT-AI 5(iii) DID NOT FULFILL THE CRITERIA FOR INCLUSION on the basis of its initial wording (77% VOTE TO INCLUDE); however, after extensive discussion and REWORDING, the consensus group unanimously supported A RE-VOTE, at which point it passed the inclusion threshold (97% TO INCLUDE)`. Both numbers published
span.quote: CONSORT-AI 5(iii) did not fulfill the criteria for inclusion on the basis of its initial wording (77% vote to include); however, after extensive discussion and rewording, the consensus group unanimously supported a re-vote, at which point it passed the inclusion threshold (97% to include).

span.label: AND THE GUIDELINE PRESCRIBES TERM GRANULARITY BY POSITION IN THE PAPER: `The title should be understandable by a wide audience; therefore, A BROADER UMBRELLA TERM such as artificial intelligence or machine learning is encouraged. MORE-PRECISE TERMS SHOULD BE USED IN THE ABSTRACT, RATHER THAN THE TITLE`. The same system is to be named at two levels of abstraction depending on where the name appears
span.quote: The title should be understandable by a wide audience; therefore, a broader umbrella term such as ‘artificial intelligence’ or ‘machine learning’ is encouraged. More-precise terms should be used in the abstract, rather than the title, unless they are broadly recognized as being a form of AI/ML. Specific terminology relating to the model type and architecture should be detailed in the abstract.

span.label: THE VOCABULARY OF THE ERA DECIDED WHAT THE SEARCH COULD FIND, AND THEY SAY SO: `the literature search of AI RCTs used terminology such as artificial intelligence, machine learning and deep learning, BUT NOT terms such as CLINICAL DECISION SUPPORT SYSTEMS or EXPERT SYSTEMS, WHICH WERE MORE COMMONLY USED IN THE 1990s for technologies underpinned by AI systems and SHARE RISKS SIMILAR TO THOSE OF RECENT EXAMPLES. IT IS LIKELY THAT SUCH SYSTEMS, IF PUBLISHED TODAY, WOULD BE INDEXED UNDER artificial intelligence OR machine learning`. A renaming across decades, named as a limitation of the guideline's own evidence base
span.quote: Second, the literature search of AI RCTs used terminology such as ‘artificial intelligence’, ‘machine learning’ and ‘deep learning’, but not terms such as ‘clinical decision support systems’ or ‘expert systems’, which were more commonly used in the 1990s for technologies underpinned by AI systems and share risks similar to those of recent examples 61 . It is likely that such systems, if published today, would be indexed under ‘artificial intelligence’ or ‘machine learning’; however, clinical decision support systems were not actively discussed during this consensus process.

span.label: A CONCEPT WAS EXCLUDED BY VOTE AND THE REASON PUBLISHED: `The topic of CONTINUOUSLY EVOLVING AI systems (ALSO KNOWN AS continuously adapting or continuously learning AI systems) was discussed at length during the consensus meeting, BUT IT WAS AGREED THAT THIS BE EXCLUDED FROM CONSORT-AI ... this field is relatively early in its development WITHOUT TANGIBLE EXAMPLES in healthcare applications`. A published statement of what the vocabulary deliberately does not cover
span.quote: The topic of ‘continuously evolving’ AI systems (also known as ‘continuously adapting’ or ‘continuously learning’ AI systems) was discussed at length during the consensus meeting, but it was agreed that this be excluded from CONSORT-AI. These are AI systems with the ability to continuously train on new data, which may cause changes in performance over time. The group noted that, while of interest, this field is relatively early in its development without tangible examples in healthcare applications, and that it would not be appropriate for it to be included in CONSORT-AI at this stage

span.label: and the checklist is explicitly a floor, not a ceiling: `these are MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS and there may be value in including ADDITIONAL ITEMS NOT INCLUDED IN THE CHECKLISTS in the report or in supplementary materials`
span.quote: It is important to note that these are minimum requirements and there may be value in including additional items not included in the checklists in the report or in supplementary materials

span.label: THE EVIDENCE BASE WAS SEVEN PAPERS: `There were 316 REGISTERED TRIALS, of which 62 were completed and 7 HAD PUBLISHED RESULTS. Two studies were reported with reference to the CONSORT statement, and one study provided an unpublished trial protocol`. A reporting standard written mostly in advance of the literature it governs
span.quote: There were 316 registered trials, of which 62 were completed and 7 had published results 30 , 38 – 43 . Two studies were reported with reference to the CONSORT statement 30 , 42 , and one study provided an unpublished trial protocol

span.label: and the reason the extension exists at all is a stated failure of the existing vocabulary: `most recent AI studies are INADEQUATELY REPORTED and EXISTING REPORTING GUIDELINES DO NOT FULLY COVER potential sources of bias specific to AI systems`
span.quote: It has been recognized that most recent AI studies are inadequately reported and existing reporting guidelines do not fully cover potential sources of bias specific to AI systems

span.label: a pre-specified 80% inclusion threshold at the consensus meeting, with anonymous electronic voting
span.note: eliminates: items entering the checklist on the strength of a loud minority - and it bound at least once: `CONSORT-AI 5(iii) DID NOT FULFILL THE CRITERIA FOR INCLUSION on the basis of its initial wording (77%)` · outcome: held
span.quote: An 80% threshold for inclusion was pre-specified and deemed reasonable by the Steering Group to demonstrate majority consensus.

span.label: a two-stage Delphi survey of 103 then 91 international stakeholders before the consensus meeting
span.note: eliminates: a checklist reflecting only the 15-person Steering Group - and 12 items came from the wider group · outcome: held
span.quote: 103 responses were received for the first Delphi round, and 91 responses (88% of participants from round one) were received for the second round. The results of the Delphi survey informed the subsequent international consensus meeting. 12 new items were proposed by the Delphi study participants and were added for discussion at the consensus meeting.

span.label: a systematic search of the trial registry for existing AI RCTs to ground the candidate items in published practice
span.note: eliminates: items invented without evidence - but it barely bound: `There were 316 REGISTERED TRIALS, of which 62 were completed and 7 HAD PUBLISHED RESULTS` · outcome: partial
span.quote: There were 316 registered trials, of which 62 were completed and 7 had published results 30 , 38 – 43 . Two studies were reported with reference to the CONSORT statement 30 , 42 , and one study provided an unpublished trial protocol

span.label: search terms covering the older names for the same technologies - `clinical decision support systems`, `expert systems`
span.note: eliminates: nothing, because they were not used: `the literature search ... used terminology such as artificial intelligence, machine learning and deep learning, BUT NOT terms such as clinical decision support systems or expert systems` · outcome: failed
span.quote: Second, the literature search of AI RCTs used terminology such as ‘artificial intelligence’, ‘machine learning’ and ‘deep learning’, but not terms such as ‘clinical decision support systems’ or ‘expert systems’, which were more commonly used in the 1990s for technologies underpinned by AI systems and share risks similar to those of recent examples 61 . It is likely that such systems, if published today, would be indexed under ‘artificial intelligence’ or ‘machine learning’; however, clinical decision support systems were not actively discussed during this consensus process.

span.label: `Health outcome` and `Clinical outcome` - TWO GLOSSARY ENTRIES WITH ONE DEFINITION, differing only in `that` versus `which`. Either they are the same concept named twice, or a distinction the authors intended did not survive into the text
span.quote: Health outcome Measured variables in the trial that are used to assess the effects of an intervention. Human–AI interaction The process of how users (humans) interact with the AI intervention, for the AI intervention to function as intended. span.label: `Performance error` - DEFINED AS DELIBERATELY UNDEFINED: `it is up to the INVESTIGATOR to specify what should be considered a performance error, preferably based on prior evidence`. The vocabulary names the slot and refuses to fill it
span.quote: Performance error Instances in which the AI intervention fails to perform as expected. This term can describe different types of failures, and it is up to the investigator to specify what should be considered a performance error, preferably based on prior evidence.

span.label: `SPIRIT-AI` - AS PRINTED IN THE GLOSSARY, THE DEFINITION OF `SPIRIT-AI extension item`, not of the initiative. The correct term is absent from the paper entirely
span.quote: SPIRIT Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials. SPIRIT-AI An additional checklist item to address AI-specific content that is not adequately covered by SPIRIT 2013. SPIRIT-AI elaboration item Additional considerations to an existing SPIRIT 2013 item when applied to AI interventions.

span.label: `AI intervention` - the load-bearing term, defined by dependence rather than by composition: `A health intervention that RELIES UPON an AI/ML component TO SERVE ITS PURPOSE`
span.quote: AI intervention A health intervention that relies upon an AI/ML component to serve its purpose.

span.label: `Development environment` versus `Operational environment` - the pair that carries the generalisation claim: the settings the training data came from, against the settings the system is deployed into
span.quote: Development environment The clinical and operational settings from which the data used for training the model is generated. This includes all aspects of the physical setting (such as geographical location, physical environment), operational setting (such as integration with an electronic record system, installation on a physical device) and clinical setting (such as primary, secondary and/or tertiary care, patient disease spectrum).
